topics.body:
# Defaults

This bundled plugin is Flash's default app knowledge. Flash itself knows no chord: every action it asks the focused app to perform (`tab_new`, `app_undo`, `app_save`, `clipboard_copy`, …) runs the binding a plugin declares for that app in `action_bindings`, unless a source such as tmux or the browsers plugin performs it first.

`defaults` declares the macOS conventions for every app — Cmd-T opens a tab, Cmd-W closes it, Cmd-1…Cmd-9 select one, Cmd-[ / Cmd-] go back and forward, Cmd-Z / Cmd-Shift-Z undo and redo, Cmd-F finds, Cmd-S saves, Cmd-P prints, Cmd-O opens, Cmd-N opens a window, Cmd-C / Cmd-X / Cmd-V use the clipboard — and the apps that differ: editors open a tab with Cmd-N, reopen one with Cmd-Shift-T and go back with Control-Minus, Messages switches conversations with Control-Tab, and Notes, TextEdit, Pages and Mail have no tabs or history at all. It also names the apps whose accessibility tree is walked only on demand.

Another plugin overrides any of these for its apps (an app-specific entry, then a matching selector, then a higher `priority` wins). Disable it with `[plugins] disabled = ["defaults"]` and those actions do nothing.
